canonical_name: LevelDB 1.23 -- log-structured merge key-value store (Jeff Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat; Google)
lineage: LSM-tree storage (O'Neil et al. 1996) as Google built it for Chrome/IndexedDB in 2011: a write-ahead log, an in-memory memtable, sorted on-disk tables, and background compaction; RECOVERY replays the log. Ancestor of RocksDB (Facebook fork, 2012).
dependencies: a C++11 compiler; tests need googletest (submodule, NOT in the release tarball -- Techne's harness replaces them)
entry_points: leveldb::DB::Open / Put / Get; db/log_reader.cc + db/db_impl.cc RecoverLogFile; db/version_set.cc compaction

example.command: cmake -DLEVELDB_BUILD_TESTS=OFF .. && make leveldb; harness: write N keys, close, reopen, read back
example.output: all keys present after reopen (log replay + table read)

upstream_docs: O'Neil, Cheng, Gawlick, O'Neil, The Log-Structured Merge-Tree, Acta Informatica 1996

human_capability_summary.built_to: absorb writes fast by appending to a log and merging later, and recover the unflushed tail of the log after a crash
human_capability_summary.pressure: write bursts, bounded memory (memtable), background compaction competing with foreground I/O, crash mid-write
human_capability_summary.success_means: every acknowledged write is readable after reopen; compaction keeps read cost bounded

known_human_problem_solved: durable ordered key-value storage under heavy write load
human_environmental_pressure: write bursts, bounded memory, crash mid-write, foreground/background contention
human_failure_condition: lost acknowledged writes after a crash, or unbounded read amplification
behavioral_entry_point: write without closing cleanly (leave the .log) and reopen; vary write_buffer_size to force memtable flushes and compactions

lineage_relations.note: human history: the fork became the mainstream LSM engine; LevelDB continues

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run leveldb-1.23
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: absorb writes fast by appending to a log and merging later, and recover the unflushed tail of the log after a crash
